Risk: Inefficient and unsafe interactions between autonomous vehicles and human drivers on roads
Problem analysis: Treating human-driven vehicles as isolated moving obstacles in planning
Theoretical insight: Robot actions influence human actions forming underactuated dynamical system
Design rationale: Plan robot trajectory by anticipating human best response to robot actions
Implementation mechanism: Model predictive control with quasi-Newton optimisation in underactuated system
Validation evidence: Simulation and offline user studies show improved coordination and efficiency
Intervention: Apply continuous inverse reinforcement learning on human driving data to learn driver reward features
Source: http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10514-018-9746-1
